summary: Counterparty-paper mutual NDA that is largely aligned but bars disclosure to advisers, auditors, insurers and affiliates, includes a residuals clause, omits two carve-outs and is narrow on compelled disclosure.

findings.quote: relating to a Party, which is disclosed or made available by or on behalf of that Party (the Disclosing Party) to the other Party (the Recipient)
findings.why: Disclosing Party and Recipient are defined so that either Party can be either, and the obligations bind both.

findings.quote: which is disclosed or made available by or on behalf of that Party (the Disclosing Party) to the other Party (the Recipient), directly or indirectly, in written, electronic, oral, visual or any other tangible or intangible form, whether before, on or after the date of this Agreement
findings.why: The definition is not tied to information disclosed for the Purpose (it expressly reaches information disclosed before the date of the Agreement and 'any and all' information), and has no marking or reasonable-expectation test.
findings.draft_redline: Confidential Information means information disclosed by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party to the Recipient for the Purpose on or after the date of this Agreement that is marked confidential or would reasonably be considered confidential, including notes and analyses derived from it.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to tie the definition to information disclosed for the Purpose and to a marked-or-reasonably-confidential test, which keeps it workable for both sides.

findings.quote: use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information solely and exclusively for the Purpose
findings.why: Use is limited solely to the Purpose, a potential commercial arrangement (the added words 'or corporate transaction' slightly widen it).

findings.quote: is received on an unrestricted basis after disclosure hereunder from an independent third party who, to the best of the Recipient's knowledge after diligent enquiry, is not under any obligation of confidentiality to the Disclosing Party in respect of such information.
findings.why: Only public domain and third-party receipt are listed; the 'already lawfully held' and 'independently developed' carve-outs are missing, and the Recipient must prove the exclusions to the Disclosing Party's reasonable satisfaction.
findings.draft_redline: Add after 3.1.2: 3.1.3 was lawfully in the Recipient's possession before disclosure by the Disclosing Party; or 3.1.4 is independently developed by or for the Recipient without use of or reference to the Confidential Information.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would be grateful if the standard exclusions for information already lawfully held and independently developed information could be added, so the exclusions work equally for both Parties.

findings.quote: The Recipient shall not disclose, transmit or make available any Confidential Information to any other person, entity or organisation whatsoever, including any external legal, financial or tax advisers, auditors, insurers, sub-contractors or corporate affiliates of the Recipient.
findings.why: Disclosure to professional advisers, auditors, insurers and Group members is expressly prohibited with no consent mechanism.
findings.draft_redline: The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information on a need-to-know basis for the Purpose to its employees, officers, directors, professional advisers, auditors, insurers and members of its Group, provided it remains liable for their compliance.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Both Parties will need to involve advisers, auditors, insurers and group companies in evaluating the Purpose, so we propose permitting need-to-know disclosure to them with the Recipient remaining responsible.

findings.quote: The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to the minimum extent required by an order of a court of competent jurisdiction or by mandatory statutory requirement
findings.why: The exception covers only court orders and statutory requirements, omitting regulators and stock exchanges; notice is 'where legally permissible' which is acceptable, but no cost allocation is stated.
findings.draft_redline: The Recipient may disclose Confidential Information to the extent required by law, court, regulator or stock exchange, giving the Disclosing Party prompt notice where legally permitted and reasonable cooperation at the Disclosing Party's cost.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like the exception to extend to regulators and stock exchange rules, with any cooperation at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: Nothing in this Agreement shall restrict or prevent the Recipient from using or developing any ideas, concepts, know-how, methods or techniques retained in the unaided memory of its personnel
findings.why: This is a residuals clause permitting use of information retained in unaided memory and excluding liability for it.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are unable to accept a residuals clause, as it would undermine the protection of each Party's confidential information; we propose deleting Clause 5.

findings.quote: the Recipient shall within five (5) Business Days:
findings.why: Five Business Days is within the accepted minimum, and confirmation is signed by an authorised officer.
findings.fallback_cited: Any period of 5 Business Days or more.

findings.quote: the Recipient may retain one archival copy of the Confidential Information solely in off-site automated disaster recovery backups, provided that such retained copies shall remain subject to the obligations of this Agreement
findings.why: Automated backups may be retained and remain confidential, though there is no express exception for copies legally required to be kept.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information, including all intellectual property rights subsisting therein, shall remain the sole and exclusive property of the Disclosing Party or its third-party licensors.
findings.why: All Confidential Information and IP stays with the Disclosing Party and no licence beyond use for the Purpose is granted (7.2).

findings.quote: All Confidential Information is furnished without warranty of any kind, whether express, implied or statutory, including warranties as to accuracy, completeness, non-infringement or fitness for purpose.
findings.why: Mutual no-warranty disclaimer in reasonable wording; Halyard gives no warranty and no fraud carve-out has been removed.
findings.fallback_cited: Mutual disclaimers in any reasonable wording.

findings.quote: shall continue in force for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party upon giving fourteen (14) days' written notice to the other Party.
findings.why: A two-year term matches; the early-termination notice is 14 days rather than 30 but termination does not end confidentiality obligations.

findings.quote: shall remain binding on the Recipient for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of termination or expiry.
findings.why: Survival of three years after expiry or termination matches the preferred position; there is no separate Trade Secret protection but this is not a listed deviation.

findings.quote: each Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief, specific performance or other equitable remedies in respect of any actual or threatened breach.
findings.why: Mutual right to seek injunctive and equitable relief.

findings.quote: constitutes the entire and whole understanding and covenant between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof
findings.why: Archaic but customary entire-agreement wording; it does not expressly exclude liability for fraud.
findings.fallback_cited: Any customary drafting, including archaic wording of standard positions.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer or subcontract any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: Mutual no assignment without prior written consent.

findings.quote: shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of England and Wales. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales
findings.why: English law and exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
